claims.text: On ghcr.io container images are stored as packages. At stage-3 both the publish job of ci.yml and release.yml are granted `packages: write`, so each can push images; a token with that permission could also push under the same name.
claims.source_hint: ci.yml lines 222-225, release.yml lines 11-13 at stage-3; GitHub docs 'Working with the Container registry' (authenticating, write:packages)

claims.text: At stage-3 envs/staging/api.yaml names the api image by a sha- tag only, without a digest.
claims.source_hint: deploy/gitops/config-repo/envs/staging/api.yaml line 42 at stage-3

claims.text: A registry assigns a digest to every image pushed, computed from the content; the digest says nothing about who pushed it.
claims.source_hint: OCI image spec 'Descriptor: digests'; Docker docs 'Image digests'

claims.text: Cosign is part of the Sigstore project, which runs the public CA (Fulcio) and transparency log (Rekor). Keyless: ephemeral key pair in memory, OIDC ID token, short-lived certificate from the CA binding the public key to the token's identity, sign, discard the private key.
claims.source_hint: docs.sigstore.dev: Cosign 'Signing with Keyless' / 'Overview' (ephemeral keys, Fulcio certificate)

claims.text: A GitHub Actions job can request an OIDC ID token only when its permissions grant `id-token: write`.
claims.source_hint: GitHub docs 'About security hardening with OpenID Connect' — Adding permissions settings

claims.text: GitHub's OIDC token is a JWT signed by the issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com; its claims include the repository, the workflow ref (workflow file) and the ref (branch) of the run.
claims.source_hint: GitHub docs 'About security hardening with OpenID Connect' — Understanding the OIDC token (iss, repository, ref, job_workflow_ref)

claims.text: Verifiers trust Sigstore's CA certificates in advance (trusted root). Fulcio checks the ID token's signature against the issuer before issuing a certificate; the certificate is valid only for minutes.
claims.source_hint: docs.sigstore.dev: Certificate Authority (Fulcio) overview — OIDC token verification, certificate validity

claims.text: For a GitHub Actions workflow the certificate's identity (SAN) is the workflow URI https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/.github/workflows/FILE@REF, and the issuer is https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com.
claims.source_hint: docs.sigstore.dev: Cosign 'Verifying Signatures' (GitHub Actions identity example); Fulcio OID/SAN docs

claims.text: Cosign records each keyless signature and its certificate in the public transparency log, and the signing also gets a trusted, signed timestamp (from the log or from a separate timestamp authority) that a verifier can check later.
claims.source_hint: docs.sigstore.dev: Cosign Verifying > Timestamps (Rekor v1 integratedTime vs Rekor v2 + TSA); Cosign 3.1 sign --use-signing-config

claims.text: Cosign stores an image's signature in the same registry repository, attached to the digest (not a tag), together with the certificate and the transparency log entry's proof, so verification can check the log entry offline.
claims.source_hint: docs.sigstore.dev: Cosign 'Signing Containers' (OCI 1.1 referrers, bundle); outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/verify-image.txt ('verified offline')

claims.text: Keyless verification checks the signature against the digest and the certificate's key, the certificate against Sigstore's CA and the expected identity and issuer, the transparency log entry, and that a trusted signed timestamp falls inside the certificate's validity window.
claims.source_hint: docs.sigstore.dev: Cosign 'Verifying Signatures'; Sigstore 'Security model' (timestamp within certificate validity)

claims.text: `cosign sign` with no `--key` signs keyless; `--yes` skips the confirmation prompt.
claims.source_hint: cosign sign --help (Cosign 3.1): -y/--yes; docs.sigstore.dev 'Signing Containers' keyless default

claims.text: ci.yml lines 264-276 at stage-3 install Cosign v3.1.3 via sigstore/cosign-installer v4.1.2 and sign `name@digest` from the push step's outputs; the publish job's matrix runs it once per image, six images.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 206-276 at stage-3

claims.text: `cosign verify` takes `--certificate-identity` and `--certificate-oidc-issuer` to name the identity and issuer a keyless certificate must carry; a looser `--certificate-identity-regexp` exists too.
claims.source_hint: cosign verify --help (Cosign 3.1); docs.sigstore.dev 'Verifying Signatures' — keyless verification flags

claims.text: verify-image.sh resolves a tag to its current digest (digest_of in scripts/lib/images.sh) and verifies the digest; with no arguments it checks the newest sha- api image, then 1.0.0; its output shows three checks and 'no signatures found' for 1.0.0.
claims.source_hint: scripts/devops/verify-image.sh lines 14-31 and 51-63, scripts/lib/images.sh, outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/verify-image.txt at stage-3

claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/verify-image.txt lines 12-16; verify-image.sh lines 55-56 comment

claims.text: release.yml at stage-3 grants only contents: write and packages: write (no id-token), runs no Cosign, and lines 46-61 fail the release when the X.Y.Z digest differs from the sha- digest.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang .github/workflows/release.yml lines 11-13, 46-61 at stage-3

claims.text: Anyone with an identity the CA accepts (e.g. a workflow in a copy of the repository under another GitHub account) can obtain a valid keyless signature for that identity.
claims.source_hint: docs.sigstore.dev: Sigstore overview / Cosign 'Verifying Signatures' (why identity must be specified)

claims.text: A signature made in release.yml would carry release.yml's identity (workflow file release.yml, tag ref), which does not match verify-image.sh's ci.yml@refs/heads/master identity.
claims.source_hint: GitHub OIDC token job_workflow_ref claim; verify-image.sh line 19

claims.text: Keyless signing leaves no long-lived signing key for the team to store, rotate or back up; trust rests on the identity check at verification.
claims.source_hint: docs.sigstore.dev: keyless signing rationale

claims.text: Cosign 3.1 uploads keyless signatures to the transparency log by default (`--tlog-upload` defaults to true and can be turned off); the log is public and append-only, so anyone can read the entries made for an identity.
claims.source_hint: cosign v3.1.3 doc/cosign_sign.md (--tlog-upload); docs.sigstore.dev Rekor overview
